reasons.plausibility: Aluminum additions to refractory high-entropy alloys can promote protective alumina scales, but in HfNbTaTiZr, Al is unlikely to form a continuous, protective Al₂O₃ layer at only 1–2 at% due to the high oxygen affinity of the base elements (Hf, Ti, Zr) and the resulting internal oxidation or mixed-oxide formation.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is clear and well-defined, directly comparing oxidation behavior and mechanical properties of baseline and Al-modified alloys under the specified conditions, with a decisive criterion for falsification.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a critical limitation of a well-known alloy with a simple, testable intervention, making it highly relevant and worth investigating despite its low scientific plausibility.
